item.title: Effective Apache .htaccess Rules for URL Trailing Slash Management
item.description:
“Effective Apache .htaccess Rules for URL Trailing Slash Management”

When configuring web servers, particularly using Apache’s .htaccess file, managing trailing slashes on URLs is crucial for SEO hygiene, canonicalization, and consistent internal linking. How can an administrator dictate whether URLs should possess a trailing slash (e.g., /page/) or strictly omit it (e.g., /page) while ensuring smooth user experience and search engine indexing?

Here are several accepted methods demonstrated through specific .htaccess configurations to achieve these distinct redirection behaviors.

item.title: Fix Apache Serving PHP Code as Text Instead of Executing It
item.description:
“Fix Apache Serving PHP Code as Text Instead of Executing It”

Encountering a situation where your web browser renders raw PHP script content instead of the processed output is a common frustration when configuring Apache web servers. This indicates that the PHP interpreter module is either not loaded, not properly configured to handle .php files, or is being overridden by another setting.

This detailed breakdown gathers various solutions that users have successfully employed across different Linux distributions and Apache versions to ensure PHP scripts execute server-side.
